tool_input.title: shop/worker OOMKilled from BATCH_SIZE env bump
tool_input.content:
Incident: KubePodCrashLooping shop/worker, cluster aurora-lab (kind-aurora-lab, cluster_id kubeconfig-2aaf9fdfbf268fbf).

**Root cause:** worker.py (mounted from configmap `api-code` in ns `shop`) allocates `BATCH_SIZE` bytearrays of 100KiB each, all held in memory simultaneously, every 5s loop. Deployment revision 2 raised `BATCH_SIZE` from 500 to 2500 without raising the container's `resources.limits.memory` (stayed at 192Mi).
- BATCH_SIZE=500 → ~48.8MiB, fits under 192Mi limit.
- BATCH_SIZE=2500 → ~244.1MiB, exceeds 192Mi limit → immediate OOMKilled (exit 137) on first batch, every restart.

**Why:** Memory limit was not scaled proportionally when BATCH_SIZE env var was bumped in a deploy. Node-level memory was never under pressure (top nodes / describe node showed <5% utilization) — this is purely a per-container cgroup limit vs demand mismatch, not a cluster capacity issue.

**How to apply / diagnose quickly next time:**
1. `kubectl get pods -n shop` — look for OOMKilled status + climbing restart count.
2. `kubectl get replicaset -n shop -l app=<deploy> -o jsonpath=...` comparing old vs new RS env/resources — reveals what changed between revisions (fast way to spot config drift causing OOM, since `kubectl rollout history` is blocked under read-only policy here).
3. Check `kubectl top nodes` / `describe node` to rule out node-level pressure before concluding container-limit OOM.
4. Fix: either revert the env var change (`kubectl set env deployment/worker BATCH_SIZE=500 -n shop`) or raise memory limit proportionally (`kubectl set resources ... --limits=memory=320Mi`) if the higher batch size is intentional.
5. General lesson: any change to a worker's batch/concurrency/buffer-size env var should be paired with a memory limit review — this app has no bound on batch-size-driven memory usage (code-level risk: worker.py has no cap on BATCH_SIZE vs available memory).
